title: Tips for Better Writing

source.name: VOA Learning English — Tips for Better Writing
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Today we continue our series of expert suggestions for academic writing. Our guest is Jennifer Ahern-Dodson, assistant professor of the Practice in Writing Studies at Duke University in North Carolina.
Ms. Ahern-Dodson starts a conversation with both students and professors planning to write a paper or essay. She asks about their earlier writing experiences. Were they negative or positive?
She advises that you are not alone if you have had problems with your writing. She says everyone struggles with writing.

“Writing is hard. All writers struggle at some point. And even if writing has come easily for you, at some point in your work as a student, that eventually you’re going to hit a roadblock. And so part of what I like to get folks thinking about is -- besides writing’s hard for everybody – is to really take a moment to think about their past writing experiences. And when the writing is going well, what was happening? When the writing wasn’t going well, what was happening?”
She says most people’s negative writing experiences happened because a very specific formula is required for a paper including an exact length.

“And so they primarily focus on, and worry about, what the final product has to look like, like how many pages for a research essay? Or if it is in the second or third language, you know, punctuation and grammar, like whether it gets communicated in the right language.
“And so focusing on the end makes it really hard to get started.”
Another problem can arise when the need to do well on a paper is extremely important.

“…like a timed essay exam, or a college application essay, or a research paper that is at the end of the semester, and it’s tied to the entire grade for the class. So worrying about what will happen if they don’t do well – get bad grades, don’t get into college -- creates, of course, significant anxiety. And that can make it harder to get the writing done.”
Then she and the people she’s helping move to more positive projects. She says usually when writing comes easily, the writers feel they have something important to say.

The teacher advises asking yourself questions. What personal understanding of the subject can you bring to your paper? Why is this subject important? For whom is it meaningful? Who will be reading it?

“…Think about who your audience is, and what it is that you really want to say to them. And what that can do is help you switch from the final product and what it can look like (to) really more on what you have to offer, your particular perspective.”
She says that is an important change for all writers.

questions.q: Why does Ms. Ahern-Dodson ask writers about their earlier experiences?
options: To help them see what changed between good and bad writing days
To decide whether they should stop writing academic papers
To check whether their grammar has improved since last year
To find out which school subjects they enjoy the most
questions.explain: Đoạn 2 và 4: bà muốn người viết nghĩ về lúc viết tốt và lúc viết không tốt; “what was happening?”.

questions.q: What does she suggest about people who find writing difficult?
options: They will improve if they practise every day
They probably began to write too late in life
Their problems are shared by writers in general
They should ask for easier topics from their teacher
questions.explain: Đoạn 3–4: “everyone struggles with writing”, “writing is hard for everybody”.

questions.q: Why can concentrating on the finished product make it hard to begin?
options: They cannot decide who their readers are going to be
They fret about how the result should look and struggle to get going
Teachers never explain how long a paper should be
They spend too long planning an interesting topic
questions.explain: Đoạn 5–7: lo về hình thức (độ dài, dấu câu, ngữ pháp) → “focusing on the end makes it really hard to get started”.

questions.q: Which writing task is most likely to produce strong anxiety?
options: A short note that a student writes to a friend
A private diary entry that nobody else will read
A practice exercise that the teacher will not grade
An essay that will help decide whether a student enters university
questions.explain: Đoạn 8–9: bài luận đăng ký đại học hoặc bài ảnh hưởng toàn bộ điểm → lo lắng nhiều (“significant anxiety”).

questions.q: In the text, “hit a roadblock” means to…
options: meet an obstacle that stops your progress
find a task easier than you expected
get an angry reply from a reader
run out of time to finish a paper
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: “hit a roadblock” = gặp trở ngại chặn tiến độ.

questions.q: What change of focus does she recommend to writers?
options: Focus less on the audience, more on the length of the paper
Focus less on the look of the paper, more on what they can offer
Focus less on grammar, more on the final grade they will get
Focus less on their own ideas, more on following the rules
questions.explain: Đoạn 11–12: chuyển từ sản phẩm cuối cùng sang điều mình có thể đóng góp, quan điểm riêng, và nghĩ về người đọc.

questions.q: She says that writers with plenty of experience never find writing hard.
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: “All writers struggle at some point”; dù viết dễ thì cũng sẽ có lúc gặp “roadblock”.

questions.q: Ms. Ahern-Dodson has published a book about academic writing.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói bà là giáo sư trợ giảng ngành Writing Studies; không nói bà xuất bản sách.

vocab.def: marks such as commas and full stops
a feeling of worry or fear
the people who read, watch or listen
a way of thinking about something

coll.ex: you’re going to hit a roadblock
writing has come easily for you

str.explain: Câu hỏi lựa chọn với or.

str.ex: even if writing has come easily for you
str.explain: even if + mệnh đề: dù điều kiện đó đúng, kết quả vẫn xảy ra.

str.ex: what it is that you really want to say to them
str.explain: Cấu trúc nhấn mạnh (cleft sentence) giúp nhấn vào phần quan trọng.
